% Problem Set 5 -- 10 problems. (Q7 is identical to PS6 Q2.)
% Do not edit except to fix statement typos.
\problemset{5}{}

\problem{5}{1}{Prove that the punctured Euclidean space $X=\R^n\setminus\{0\}$ is path
connected if and only if $n>1$.}

\problem{5}{2}{Prove that $\R^2\setminus\Q^2$ with the subspace topology of $\R^2$ is
connected, but $\R\setminus\Q$ with the subspace topology of $\R$ is not connected.}

\problem{5}{3}{Let $X$ and $Y$ be topological spaces, and suppose there exist embeddings
$f\colon X\to Y$ and $g\colon Y\to X$. Is it necessary that $X$ and $Y$ are homeomorphic?
Prove or provide a counterexample.}

\problem{5}{4}{Let $X$ be a non-empty topological space and let $\B$ be a base for the
topology on $X$. Prove that $X$ is compact if and only if every open cover of $X$ consisting
of elements of $\B$ has a finite subcover.}

\problem{5}{5}{Let $\T_1$ and $\T_2$ be two topologies on $X$ such that both $(X,\T_1)$ and
$(X,\T_2)$ are compact Hausdorff spaces. Prove that either $\T_1=\T_2$ or they are not
comparable.}

\problem{5}{6}{Prove that every compact subspace of a metric space is closed and bounded in
that metric topology. Find an example of a metric space in which a closed and bounded
subspace is not compact.}

\problem{5}{7}{Let $X$ be a compact metric space. Prove that if $f\colon X\to X$ is an
isometry (distance preserving map) of $X$, then $f$ is a homeomorphism.}

\problem{5}{8}{Let $\R$ be given the cocountable topology. Is the closed interval $[0,1]$ a
compact subspace of $\R$ under this topology?}

\problem{5}{9}{Let $f\colon X\to Y$ be a continuous map between topological spaces. Show that
if $X$ is compact and $Y$ is Hausdorff, then $f$ is a closed map.}

\problem{5}{10}{Prove that if $Y$ is compact, then the projection
$\pi_X\colon X\times Y\to X$ is a closed map.}
